The TSV, docs/map-review.html, scenes/maps/, docs/, bench/, src/, and assets/ are unchanged in the whole range (git diff --exit-code empty), so Phase 2 changed no map, no TSV row, and no mockup, exactly as the plan designs it. All gates were rerun live and pass: check-review.sh exits 0 with 34 checks (PASS=34, FAIL=0), matching plan.md:57-58 word for word; adversarial-p2.sh exits 0 with the control at 34 of 34, every gate probe CAUGHT, and probe 06 informational as recorded; the plan gate ls lists exactly four vision-review JSON files. Every plan evidence claim at plan.md:37, 42, and 52 to 75 was re-verified against live command output, including the Red exit 1 with 8 FAILs in red-p2.log, the by-design check-inventory.sh failure at 96 checks (PASS=6, FAIL=90), the mill row at inventory.md line 39 holding Judge rating 5.5 and Judge critical true with state rated, and the disposition facts: scenes/maps/bank.ts line 4 places the three chandeliers at y=2, assets/watermill.ts line 20 sets the wheel at WCX=1.15 and line 116 builds the radius-1.2 rim, so the mill rework is a yaw or camera fix and the wheel is not rebuilt. Orchestrator disposition sufficiency: sufficient. The UX spot-check FAIL names one judge-note inaccuracy (bank) with zero rating and zero bar impact (judge 7.5, spot check 7.5, bar outcome unchanged on all 8 samples, no critical missed), the disposition keeps the judge files as true records of what the judge wrote (rewriting them would falsify evidence), records the correction in plan.md:66-75 under the commit 56bdd0cf, and preserves the escalation path (the plan header says the PM may reverse each decision). The disposition changes no phase outcome: bank stays above the bar either way, and mill stays in the Phase 3 rework set either way (5.5 and critical true). Review currency: Reviews A and C at c095ba1f still cover the phase and must not run again. Every commit after c095ba1f (6e9cb9b7, 36dec52e, 0aed743a, 56bdd0cf, b78fdde1) touches only measure/runs/ and the plan evidence text: the implementation content (scenes/inventory.md, the eight vision-review files, the TSV, the map sources) is byte-identical at HEAD, the one reviewed test file that changed (check-review.sh at 36dec52e) is the remediation of review-a F1 and F2, and that change is covered by the adversarial re-audit PASS at 36dec52e and by this acceptance's own live gate reruns. The plan.md reflow after c095ba1f kept every quoted claim intact and added only the disposition block. Route substitution noted: ra-quota pick vision-review offers no route outside the claude and kimi families, so the four judge batches and the spot check ran on kimi-code-plan-cn/kimi-for-coding; the kimi family differs from the maker family Anthropic Sonnet, which is the requirement the spec and the checker enforce, and the substitution is recorded in ux-browser-review-p2-0aed743.json route_note. Four Nits carry forward, none blocking: ADV-4 (the log citation check never compares the cited model value with the batch route or family), the fixture-tree ancestor skip (ADV-P2-06 informational, defense proven on the real tree), the Phase 3 by-design note that check-review.sh P2-d will fail when state cells change, and the standing ux JSON status fail with escalate_human that the plan disposition supersedes.
nonblocking_findings: F1 [Nit] phase-acceptance (carried from adversarial ADV-4 at 36dec52e, reconfirmed by this audit): the P2-c log check in check-review.sh requires a labeled model_id or model_family line but never compares the cited value with the batch route or model family, so a log citing model_id: claude-sonnet-5-5 passes the gate (adversarial R4 fixture). The committed logs are true records: grep finds model_id: kimi-for-coding exactly once in each of vision-review-b1.log to b4.log, so the exposure is future drift only. Route to Red as a follow-up the next time the Phase 3 checker work touches check-review.sh, taking care not to reintroduce the substring vacuity that ADV-P2-03 exposed.

F2 [Nit] phase-acceptance (carried from adversarial ADV-P2-06, informational): the audited_head ancestor check in check-review.sh is skipped by design in a fixture tree with no git HEAD, so adversarial-p2.sh will keep printing DEFECT CONFIRMED (informational) for probe 06. The defense is proven on real trees: the adversarial R1 probe mutated the live batch audited_head, the checker failed with an exact P2-c FAIL line, and the file was restored byte-identical. All four committed batches record audited_head 3b35a490 and this audit re-ran git merge-base --is-ancestor 3b35a490 b78fdde1 live: it is an ancestor of HEAD.

F3 [Nit] phase-acceptance (carried from review-a F3 at c095ba1f): check-review.sh P2-d asserts the Phase 2 state cell rated, so it will fail by design in Phase 3 when reworked rows change state, in the same way check-inventory.sh now fails by design (plan.md:63-65 records that failure correctly). The plan should add the analogous by-design note for check-review.sh when Phase 3 runs, so the Phase 3 gate runner does not mistake the expected failure for a regression.

F4 [Nit] phase-acceptance: ux-browser-review-p2-0aed743.json keeps status fail with retry_recommendation escalate_human, and the orchestrator disposition supersedes it in plan.md:66-75 (commit 56bdd0cf) without editing the UX artifact. This is consistent because the JSON records the spot check's own verdict rule (a judge note must match the shots) while the plan records the owner-level disposition, and no gate reads the UX status. A later reader aggregating UX statuses should read the plan disposition alongside the JSON.
